item.title: NCP names mayoral candidates for Dhaka city polls
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has announced its mayoral candidates for the two Dhaka city corporations.
The party named Nasiruddin Patwary as its candidate for Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and Asif Mahmud for Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC).
Party convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam announced the names on Sunday afternoon at an exchange meeting with potential councilor candidates from different wards of Dhaka South and North city corporations at the NCP office.
Earlier, the party had planned to field Asif Mahmud for Dhaka South and Ariful Islam Adib for Dhaka North.
At the meeting, Nahid Islam provided guidelines to potential councilor candidates from different wards of the 2 metropolitan areas. He instructed them to search for potential councilor candidates, identify ward-based civic problems, maintain regular contact with the families of July martyrs and those injured, and closely monitor sabotage activities by the ousted and absconding Awami League.
Isahak Sarkar and Ariful Islam Adib, conveners of the South and North metropolitan units respectively, along with leaders from different levels, were present at the meeting.

item.title: State Minister Tuku: Dengue crisis may worsen in coming months
item.description:
State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salauddin Tuku has said the ongoing dengue situation in Dhaka and other districts could take a more alarming turn over the coming months, urging citizens to remain vigilant from now.
"The risk of dengue may increase further in the coming months, so everyone needs to become aware from now," Tuku said while addressing a views exchange meeting with lawmakers and administration on the overall law and order situation and development activities in Dhaka district, held at the Dhaka Deputy Commissioner's conference room.
The state minister said public representatives, the administration and local residents must work together to combat dengue through cleanliness drives, destruction of mosquito breeding grounds and heightened public awareness.
On law and order in the capital, Tuku said maintaining law and order is not the administration's responsibility alone.
A safe and stable society, he said, can only be built through the coordinated efforts of political leadership, the administration, law enforcement agencies and the general public.
Noting that the government is working to keep the country's law and order situation normal while advancing development activities, he called for effective coordination among the district administration, police administration and public representatives, adding that obstacles to development work must be identified and addressed alongside maintaining law and order.
He stressed the need for special surveillance to prevent various criminal activities in the capital and its surrounding areas, particularly in crime-prone zones, calling for increased law enforcement activity and greater political and social awareness in those areas.
Describing drugs as a major threat to society that is drawing in people from all walks of life, Tuku said the administration, public representatives and social organisations must play a more active role in curbing the spread of narcotics.
Addressing government officials, the state minister said that as state functionaries, they must carry out their duties giving top priority to public welfare and state interests, stressing that all administrative activities should be conducted in the interest of the state and the people, not any individual or group.
The meeting was chaired by Dhaka Deputy Commissioner Farida Khanom. State Minister for the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain attended as special guest.
Also present were Chief Whip of the Opposition Nahid Islam, Dhaka-12 MP Saiful Alam Khan Milon, reserved women's seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed, Superintendent of Police Shamima Parveen, representatives of various law enforcement agencies, local government officials, public representatives and members of the district law and order committee.

item.title: Minister: No child to be deprived of education due to financial hardship
item.description:
Food Minister Afroza Khanam Rita on Sunday said the government is giving due importance to ensuring that no child is deprived of education due to financial hardship.
“Government assistance and various welfare programs will continue in the future to ensure educational opportunities for children from poor and disadvantaged families,” she said.
She made the remarks while addressing a function to distribute school uniforms among students at Betila Government Primary School as the chief guest.
The minister said ensuring quality education and necessary facilities for students is essential to building an educated, humane and discrimination-free society. The present government is working to establish a social and humane state, she added.
As part of these efforts, various programs are being implemented to encourage students in their studies, provide educational materials and facilitate their education, the minister said.
Afroza said improvements in the quality of education would accelerate the country’s progress. Today’s students will play an important role in running the country in the future. Therefore, creating a quality educational environment and ensuring conditions conducive to the development of their intellect and creativity are important responsibilities of the state, she added.
The food minister urged the students to attend school regularly and study attentively.
She also called upon teachers to teach with sincerity and responsibility while helping develop the students’ moral and humanitarian values.
Deputy Commissioner of the district Nazmun Ara Sultana chaired the program. Police Super Mohammad Sarwar Alam, relevant district and upazila-level officials, local leaders, teachers, guardians and students were, among others, present.
Later, the Betila Union BNP and its affiliated and associate organizations organized a mass reception for the food minister on the same school ground. Syed Maksudul Hasan Chowdhury presided over the reception.

item.title: ACC probes new allegations against Asif Mahmud
item.description:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has decided to add a new set of allegations against former adviser Asif Mahmud to its ongoing inquiry into alleged financial transactions involving appointments and postings, commissions from development projects and tenders, bribery and money laundering.
ACC Deputy Director and Public Relations Officer Aktarul Islam disclosed the information at a press conference on Sunday.
Aktarul Islam said the new application contains allegations of irregularities and financial transactions involving the appointment of an administrator to Dhaka North City Corporation, the posting of deputy commissioners (DCs) in different districts, tender processes at Dhaka South City Corporation and other agencies, and development projects under the Ministry of Local Government.
According to the application submitted to the ACC, about Tk 60cr allegedly changed hands in the appointment of an administrator to Dhaka North City Corporation, while Tk 2cr to Tk 10cr per person was allegedly transacted in the posting of DCs in 36 districts.
Aktarul Islam said the allegations are being investigated.
The application also alleges that while Asif Mahmud was responsible for the Ministry of Local Government, he received commissions ranging from 10% to 30% from tenders for various development projects.
It also alleges his involvement in irregularities in tender processes at Dhaka South City Corporation, Narayanganj City Corporation and Comilla City Corporation.
The application further alleges that a large amount of money was embezzled by increasing the costs of rural infrastructure development and bridge construction projects under the Ministry of Local Government.
It also alleges an unusual increase in the cost of the 3rd phase of the Dhaka Water Supply and Sewerage Authority’s Sayedabad Water Treatment Plant project and an increase of nearly Tk 1,200cr in the cost of the Sheikh Russel Mini Stadium project to allegedly misappropriate money.
The application also contains allegations of transactions involving crores of taka in various appointments, transfers and promotions under the Ministry of Youth and Sports.
It alleges that Tk 10cr was taken as a bribe in exchange for appointing Abdus Salam as managing director of Dhaka Water Supply and Sewerage Authority, Tk 52cr was paid as a bribe for appointing former Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) chief engineer Md Abdur Rashid Khan, and Tk 65cr was transacted to appoint Abdul Latif Khan as chief executive officer of Gazipur City Corporation.
The application also raises allegations concerning Asif Mahmud’s lifestyle and acquisition of assets abroad. It claims that he regularly visited 5-star hotels, lived in a luxurious flat, used expensive cars and traveled by helicopter, resulting in the misuse of state funds.
It further alleges that land was purchased in Portugal, investments were made in a company in Dubai and money was deposited in Swiss banks with funds allegedly acquired through corruption.
The application claims that Tk 4,500cr was siphoned off to Dubai, Tk 3,000cr to Singapore, Tk 2,000cr to Australia and Tk 1,500cr to Switzerland, where assets were purchased and investments were made in various businesses.
It also alleges that money was laundered abroad through the husbands of 2 sisters and a nephew.
The ACC said the figures concerning money laundering and claims about assets are allegations made by the applicant. Their veracity is being verified through the inquiry.
The application also mentions an allocation of Tk 453cr for Asif Mahmud’s home upazila of Muradnagar under a rural infrastructure development project. The complainant claims the process of allocation and receipt of the funds under the project is questionable.
It also alleges that Asif Mahmud’s father Billal Hossain and his assistant private secretary (APS) Moazzem Hossain controlled a syndicate of contractors and collected money by influencing the local administration.
His personal officer (PO) Mahfuzul Alam Bhuiyan has also been accused of lobbying for bribery transactions and abusing power.
ACC Public Relations Officer Aktarul Islam said an inquiry into allegations of corruption and irregularities against Asif Mahmud had already been ongoing. He said the new allegations would be attached to the previous documents and investigated.
On September 2, ACC official Akhtarul Islam said at a press conference that the commission had found “initial evidence” of allegations of irregularities in transfers, appointments and promotions involving former adviser Asif Mahmud .
Following those remarks, the issue was widely circulated in various media outlets and on social media.
Asif Mahmud held a press conference that day to protest the allegations. On Thursday, Supreme Court lawyer Muhammad Rafiqul Islam Joni sent a notice to the ACC on his behalf.
The National Citizens Party (NCP) confirmed the matter in a statement sent to the media on Friday.
On the next working day, the ACC announced that it had received new allegations against Asif Mahmud and would investigate them.

item.title: DNCC fines Tk 1.77 lakh over Aedes larvae in Dhaka homes
item.description:
The Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) has realised Tk1,77,500 in fines from 28 cases after Aedes mosquito larvae were found in several households across various areas under its jurisdiction.
DNCC executive magistrates conducted mobile court drives in different areas on Sunday as part of a three-month-long mosquito eradication program, imposing the fines after detecting Aedes larvae on the premises of various homes.
The cases were filed in Mirpur-10, Rupnagar, Uttar Pallabi, Agargaon, Uttara Nikunjo and Baridhara areas, DNCC said.
The mobile courts were led by DNCC-appointed executive magistrates Atish Darshi Chakma, SM Rasel Islam Noor, Shariful Alam Tanvir, Pramotha Ranjan Ghatak and Dedarul Islam.
The drive comes under a three-month campaign announced by the Prime Minister on National Dengue Prevention Day.

item.title: Hajj-2027 registration ends on Sept 24
item.description:
The registration process for the 2027 Hajj will end on September 24 this year, with no scope for an extension, according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
As per instructions from the Saudi government, immediately after the registration process ends, the final number of Hajj pilgrims from Bangladesh will be communicated to the Saudi authorities.
Based on the final number of pilgrims, necessary activities, including remittance of funds for the Saudi phase, medical checkups, fitness certificates, vaccination, and training programs, will be carried out.
Bangladesh’s Hajj quota for 2027 is 78,500 pilgrims. As of September 9, 2026, a total of 3,741 pilgrims have registered, including 1,065 through the government channel and 2,676 through the private channel.
All concerned have been requested to complete registration within the stipulated deadline of September 24 to ensure their participation in the 2027 Hajj in accordance with the instructions of the Saudi government.
The registration process for Hajj 2027 began on July 27 this year.

item.title: PM for reducing import dependence by boosting farm production
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday stressed the need to reduce Bangladesh’s dependence on imports of agricultural and food products by increasing domestic production of crops that can be grown in the country.
He also asked officials of the Ministry of Agriculture to take effective measures to boost the production of locally viable agricultural commodities, while ensuring food security and making farming more productive and profitable, said a release issued by the PM’s Press Wing.
The prime minister gave the directives at a meeting with officials of the ministry at its conference room in the Bangladesh Secretariat in the afternoon.
He directed officials to focus not only on increasing agricultural productivity but also on reducing farmers’ production costs and ensuring fair prices for their produce.
“We must gradually reduce our dependence on imports of agricultural and food products that can be produced domestically. To this end, we need to put greater emphasis on increasing domestic production by quickly taking research findings, improved varieties, modern technologies, irrigation facilities and mechanization to farmers,” Tarique Rahman said.
Earlier, the prime minister walked from his office to the agriculture ministry and took the stairs instead of using the lift to reach the ministry’s conference room.
At the meeting, officials presented the overall situation of the agriculture sector, ongoing activities of the ministry and its plans.
The ministry informed the meeting that mustard production has increased significantly as part of efforts to reduce dependence on imported edible oil.
Mustard production rose from 8.24 lakh tonnes in 2021-22 to 15.34 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 and 15.41 lakh tonnes in 2025-26.
The meeting was also informed of initiatives to increase onion production and storage capacity. “Measures include introducing air-flow technology for onion storage at farmers’ level and expanding summer onion varieties.”
The ministry is also working to expand climate-resilient crop varieties tolerant to salinity, drought and waterlogging at the field level.
Highlighting progress in agricultural research, officials said a total of 1,090 crop varieties have so far been developed, including 155 rice varieties.
More than 1,000 agricultural technologies have also been developed, according to the presentation.
The meeting stressed greater emphasis on agricultural mechanization to reduce labour and production costs while increasing productivity.
The government is working to increase domestic production of agricultural machinery and make equipment such as combine harvesters, reapers and rice transplanters available to farmers at affordable prices.
The expansion of solar-powered irrigation was also discussed. There are currently 2,617 solar irrigation systems in the country, and expanding renewable energy-based irrigation could help reduce farmers’ irrigation costs and dependence on conventional fuels, officials said.
The meeting also reviewed the Farmers’ Card program aimed at ensuring direct delivery of government support to farmers.
The agriculture ministry has set a target of bringing 43 lakh farmers under the card program in the 2026-27 fiscal year. Preparations are underway to distribute cards to around 1.10 lakh farmers in the first phase, the meeting was informed.
The meeting also discussed canal excavation, tree plantation, and storage and marketing of farm produce.

item.title: Ten rescued after boat capsizes in Padma, including 20-day-old baby
item.description:
A 20-day-old baby was among 12 people swept into the Padma River after a boat capsized in Chapainawabganj on Saturday, with 10 Bangladeshis later rescued by India's Border Security Force (BSF) and one person still missing.
The boat capsized around 5:30pm while travelling from Bakherali to Johurpur Belpara in Chapainawabganj Sadar as the river became rough. The baby, Tanisha, was travelling in her mother Tania Khatun's arms when the boat sank and all 12 people on board fell into the water.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Md Wasim, 23, managed to swim to the shore, while the remaining 11 passengers went missing.
Amid the strong current and storm, the passengers tried to stay afloat by holding onto the boat’s wooden floor, sacks, floating pieces of wood, paddles and other objects.
Tania Khatun held Tanisha tightly, but at one point the strong current pulled the baby from her arms. Tania later found Tanisha underwater and held her tightly again.
Tanisha’s maternal grandfather Ibrahim also swam while holding the baby above the water with one hand.
After floating in the water for around 1 hour and 20 minutes, the current carried them towards Indian waters. BSF members spotted 10 Bangladeshis, including Tanisha, and went to rescue them in a speedboat before taking them to the riverbank.
At the time of the rescue, 20-day-old Tanisha was almost unresponsive after swallowing water while being held by her mother. BSF members quickly took her to a local medical centre, where doctors examined her and said she was healthy.
The incident occurred while the group was travelling from Bakherali in Chapainawabganj Sadar to Johurpur Belpara. Tanisha is the daughter of Md Sohel and Tania Khatun of Johurpur Belpara in Sadar upazila.
Shariful Islam, subedar of the Bakher Ali Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) camp, said rescuers told him that Tania had been holding Tanisha tightly after the boat sank.
He said: “They floated by holding onto the boat’s rice husk, paddle and wooden floor. At one point, the strong current pulled the child from her mother’s hand and she sank into the water. Later, Tania Khatun found her and held her tightly again.”
Shahidul Islam, company commander of Faridpur Border Outpost (BOP), said Tanisha’s maternal grandfather knew how to swim, while the women stayed afloat by holding onto the boat’s wooden floor, paddles and sacks.
He said: “They remained floating in the water for more than an hour.”
Rabiul Islam Rabu, member of Ward 8 of Narayanpur Union Parishad, said Tania initially held Tanisha tightly, but the strong current and storm caused the baby to slip from her arms and sink.
He said Tania later found Tanisha and held her above the water with her legs. Seeing the baby in distress, her grandfather Ibrahim held her above the water with 1 hand while swimming to survive.
Rabiul Islam Rabu said they remained in the water for around 1 hour and 20 minutes before BSF members rescued them.
Shyamalal Mondal, a resident of Taranagar in Lalbagh police station area of Murshidabad district, was present on the Indian side when the BSF rescued the Bangladeshis.
He said BSF members rescued the Bangladeshis and took them to the riverbank. He added that 20-day-old Tanisha was almost unresponsive at the time and that BSF members immediately took her to a local medical center, where doctors said she was healthy.
Lieutenant Colonel Kazi Mostafizur Rahman, commander of BGB’s 53 Battalion, said members of the BSF’s 71 Battalion Khandua Camp rescued the Bangladeshis with a speedboat on Saturday night.
He said the BSF handed over the 10 rescued Bangladeshis to the BGB that night, after which the BGB released them into the custody of their relatives.
Kazi Mostafizur Rahman said 9 of the 10 rescued Bangladeshis, including Tanisha, returned home that night in healthy condition.
At around 5pm on Saturday, a motorized boat carrying 12 passengers left Alimnagar Ghat in the Bakherali area for Johurpurtek village. The boat sank in the Padma River on the way.
At around 5:50pm, the company commander of the 71 Battalion BSF’s Khandua Camp informed the BGB about the boat sinking. He said the BSF had rescued 10 Bangladeshis alive, including 4 men, 3 women and 3 children.
The Chapainawabganj Battalion, 53 BGB, then took steps to bring them back to Bangladesh. At 9:55pm, a company commander-level flag meeting was held between the commander of Faridpur BOP and the commander of the Khandua BSF Camp.
Following the meeting, the 10 rescued Bangladeshis were brought back to Bangladesh. They were later handed over to their close relative, Md Ismail Hossain, in the presence of local public representatives.
The BGB said all the rescued people were in good health.
The rescued people were Md Russell, 26; Md Ibrahim, 50; Sowdagar, 40; Md Ibrahim, 60; Sakhina, 45; Nilufta, 35; Tania, 22, and her 20-day-old daughter; Sanaullah, 9; and Al Amin, 9.
All of them are from Johurpur (Bokaripara) village in Chapainawabganj.
Meanwhile, Md Mostafa, 60, son of late Altab Hossain, from the same village, remains missing. Search and rescue operations are continuing to locate him.

item.title: The RYZE of Bangladesh’s first AI Hub
item.description:
Artificial Intelligence has become deeply entwined within education, the arts, wellbeing, and everyday life. Consequently, access to different AI tools has become a daily requirement and an important part of the user experience. However, using multiple platforms simultaneously can be a hassle; switching between apps, managing separate subscriptions, and dealing with international payments.
Banglalink took the step towards simplifying AI access, bringing together multiple leading Artificial Intelligence models within its AI-powered digital lifestyle brand, RYZE. Incorporating ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Claude and Gemini within one interface, RYZE’s aim is to simplify access to advanced AI tools for everyday users, students, and professionals.
The RYZE AI Hub was initially soft launched in January this year during a freshers’ orientation programme at BRAC University by Banglalink’s CEO, Johan Buse. It was officially launched in April, marking its wider availability and giving users the chance to select models suited to different tasks, whether writing, research or other activities.
The focus on practical skills and employability has also brought international recognition. RYZE received the AI Innovation Award at the Global Conference on AI Leadership and Flagship Prestige Awards 2026 for its contribution to advancing AI solutions aimed at improving young people's skills and employability. The recognition came within the same year as the AI Hub’s commercial launch.
RYZE’s access model is also different from quintessential subscription approaches. Users get access to premium AI models by purchasing tokens and using them according to requirements rather than taking separate monthly subscriptions. The hassle of payment through dollar endorsed credit card is also removed as users are allowed to pay via local mobile financial services. Moreover, RYZE is not limited to users of one mobile network; it is a telco-agnostic platform that can be accessed by users across networks.
Users receive free 10,000 tokens upon signing up and do so each month for basic use. Additional tokens are available upon purchasing RYZE’s In-App Packs- Core, Pro, Max and Ultra. These packs offer 100,000, 210,000, 575,000, and 1,250,000 tokens respectively, each valid for 30 days.
For users in Bangladesh, the payment mechanism is another practical consideration, reflective of Banglalink’s commitment to care.
Access to many international digital services can be complicated by the need for an internationally enabled credit or debit card. Along with traditional payment methods, RYZE also allows users to purchase tokens through local mobile financial services such as bKash or Nagad.
As AI becomes increasingly relevant to learning and professional life, the evolution of platforms like RYZE suggests that the next question for Bangladesh may not simply be whether people can use AI, but how easily they can access the tools they need.

item.title: Harun’s family receives PM’s gift 12 years after his death
item.description:
More than 12 years after Jubo Dal leader Mohammad Harunur Rashid was killed in police firing in Feni, his family has finally received a new home.
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi handed over the keys to the newly built house to Harunur’s family at Jagatjibanpur in Farhadnagar Union of the district on Sunday. His wife, Bibi Zohra, daughter Majeda Akter and son Touhidul Islam received the keys.
According to district BNP sources, Harunur was killed in police firing on December 4, 2013, amid tensions surrounding a BNP-led programme in support of a hartal on Shaheed Shahidullah Kaiser Road in Feni town. He was then vice-president of the Farhadnagar Union Jubo Dal.
After his death, his wife and children endured years of hardship, including uncertainty over their livelihood and housing.
The new house was built in Jagatjibanpur under an initiative of “Amra BNP Poribar” to rehabilitate the family, following instructions from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. Construction began on April 12.
Speaking at the key handover ceremony, Ruhul Kabir Rizvi accused the previous Awami League government of enforced disappearances and killings.
“Sheikh Hasina did not hesitate to kill anyone to consolidate power. Enforced disappearances and killings continued for 17 years,” he said.
Local BNP leaders recalled Harunur’s political contributions and pledged to continue supporting his family.
The family expressed relief after finally receiving a secure home following years of housing difficulties, though the loss of their husband and father continues to leave a deep void in their lives.
After the ceremony, Rizvi visited Harunur’s grave and inaugurated the nameplate of the new house.

item.title: Government primary schools in Dhaka face enrolment decline
item.description:
On a school day, rows of empty benches outnumbered students at Swamibag Government Primary School in Dhaka, where only a few children were present during scheduled class hours.
At around 10am, three children were seen sitting in one classroom without a teacher. By around 1pm, the few students who remained had left, saying classes were over.
On another day, five students were present. However, government records show that the school has 58 students and 5 teachers.
The contrast between official records and what is visible inside classrooms is not limited to one school.
Over three days, Dhaka Tribune visited several government primary schools in Dhaka’s Sutrapur area, including Government Colony Primary, Swamibag Primary, Bongobashi Government Primary, Muslim Government and Narinda primary schools, at different times between 10am and noon.
Photo: Asiful Islam Rifat/Dhaka Tribune
The visits found classrooms with very few students, aging infrastructure, stagnant water, unclean surroundings, and limited space for children to play.
The gap between official data and ground reality extends to several other government primary schools in the area, including Bangla Bazar, Bongobashi, Muslim and Wari Mohila Somity primary schools.
Sutrapur Thana has 48 government primary schools, 322 working teachers, and 8,274 enrolled students.
Data shows low enrolment at several institutions. Muslim Government Primary School has 23 enrolled students for 4 teachers, Bongobashi Government Primary School lists 26 students for 3 teachers, Nobendro Boshak Lane Government Primary School has 32 students; and Narinda Mohila Somity Government Primary School reports 40 students.
However, the figures do not tell the whole story.
At Swamibag Government Primary School, official records list 58 students and five working teachers against six approved posts. Government data also shows that the school has nine classrooms, three toilets and a safe drinking water source.
During two separate visits, however, only three and five students, respectively, were seen at the school. Some classrooms were covered in dust, while waterlogging made parts of the school unsuitable for classes.
Photo: Asiful Islam Rifat/Dhaka Tribune
Addressing the discrepancy, Samina Yasmin, headteacher of Swamibag Government Primary School, said: “We have continuously informed the senior authorities about the structural issues at the school. They are well aware of the issue. Our teachers repeatedly encourage students to attend school and communicate with parents, but many children attend for a few days before becoming irregular again.”
She defended the teaching staff while acknowledging the attendance problems.
“We take classes regularly. But when there are no students, what classes can we take?” she added.
Kishori Rani Biswas, headteacher of Bongobashi Government Primary School, said: “Since I joined the school, I have tried my best to improve the situation. Currently, 33 students are enrolled here. We are continuously working to gradually increase the number of students.”
The problem is not limited to attendance. Plaster on the entrance walls was peeling off, revealing damp and weathered brickwork. The narrow passage leading inside was littered with debris and stagnant water.
Broken bricks, rubbish and stagnant water were visible in different areas of the premises. Moss had accumulated along parts of the boundary wall and in narrow spaces behind classrooms.
Classrooms were covered in dust and contained only a few broken benches and a fractured wallboard.
A significant portion of the school premises was waterlogged, with dark, dirty rainwater standing for extended periods. The stagnant water was accompanied by mosquitoes.
Photo: Asiful Islam Rifat/Dhaka Tribune
The surroundings of school equipment also appeared poorly maintained.
Similar problems were observed at Government Colony Primary School and most of the other schools visited in the area. In several places, aging buildings, limited open space and poor cleanliness were visible.
For many families, government primary schools remain an affordable option. But parents interviewed during the field visits said low cost alone was no longer enough to convince them to choose these schools.
Subhan Rahman, a guardian of two children, said the facilities and classroom environment were not satisfactory.
“The facilities are not very good. Classes are also not always held properly. That is why many people are not interested in sending their children here,” he said.
Farida Yasmin pointed to another problem, describing a cycle in which declining attendance further weakens the school environment.
“Classes are not always held regularly, and the infrastructure is also unsatisfactory. Besides, it creates a cycle. There are fewer students, so there is less activity in the classroom. Again, because the environment is not good, new students do not come,” she said.
Sharmin Sultana, a resident of the area, has not sent either of her two children to a government primary school. Instead, both attend a private institution.
For her, the decision was not simply about academic considerations.
“The school has transport and other facilities, which is important for working mothers. I don’t have to worry about taking my children to and from school,” she said.
“Private institutions follow a more up-to-date curriculum and provide greater individual attention to students,” she added.
Highlighting the systemic nature of the issue, educationist Prof Dr Manzoor Ahmed said affluent and middle-class urban families have long shifted away from government primary institutions.
Emphasizing that physical access alone cannot sustain enrollment without quality and safety, he said: “Dilapidated infrastructure, teacher shortage, security concerns, teaching methods, lack of play areas, and the absence of individualized learning support are driving parents away from government primary schools.”
Commenting on the structural deficiencies, Nahida Sultana, assistant thana education officer (ATEO) of Sutrapur, told Dhaka Tribune: “We are aware of the infrastructural issues in several schools under our jurisdiction. We have documented these concerns and submitted requests for necessary allocations to the higher authorities. Once funds are sanctioned, renovation and infrastructure improvement works will begin.”
She acknowledged administrative shortages, saying: “Some of the schools lack headteachers and assistant headteachers.”
She added: “Although student numbers are low due to parental reluctance, we are actively working to raise awareness among them. We are conducting cluster-based monitoring and submit weekly reports. If any teacher is found negligent in performing their classroom duties upon investigation, strict action will be taken.”
At a recent press conference, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj said monitoring should not rely only on administrative reports and paperwork but should be based on actual results. On the declining attendance of students, Bobby Hajjaj told Dhaka Tribune: “We are trying to understand and meet the needs of parents and students and take measures accordingly. Government facilities are meant for the people. Our effort will be to understand what people want and find ways to meet those needs. If we fail to meet their needs, government primary schools will eventually be closed."
Asked about the government’s plans for the schools’ infrastructure, he said: “Yes, I am aware of the condition of the buildings. We are working to modernize these buildings, and hopefully, the work will begin by the end of this year or early next year.”
Educationists say government primary schools remain one of the few affordable avenues for formal education for many low-income families in Dhaka. If these institutions continue to lose students while private alternatives expand, the issue could affect access to affordable and equitable education in the capital.
